st: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a 9x9-inch baking dish with [[1 tbsp]] butter.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a skillet and cook the onions for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Let them cool.
In a large bowl cream the remaining [[3 tbsp]] butter until smooth, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Stir in the milk, cottage cheese, cooked onions and crumbled cheese.
Add the cornmeal, salt and baking powder and fold until just combined. The batter should be thick but pourable.
Pour into the dish and bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the top is golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool for 10 minutes, then cut into squares. Serve warm as a side.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Beat the butter, salt and anise seeds together in a large bowl until creamy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the grated cheese.
Mix in the cassava starch and milk and knead by hand for 3 minutes until it forms a soft, smooth dough. Add 1 tablespoon more milk if it cracks.
Rest the dough for 10 minutes.
Roll pieces into small rings or balls about 2 inches wide and place them on the sheet.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until puffed and pale golden. Serve warm; they are best the same day.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a 9x13-inch dish with [[1 tbsp]] butter.
Melt [[3 tbsp]] butter in a skillet and cook the onion for 7 minutes until soft.
Blend the corn with the milk until mostly smooth but still a little textured.
Stir the corn mixture, onions, cornmeal, cheese, egg yolks and salt in a large bowl.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks in a clean bowl, then gently fold them into the batter.
Pour into the dish and bake for 45 to 50 minutes until set and golden on top.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting into squares.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, pepper and garlic for 5 minutes.
Add the tomato, carrots, oregano and [[1.5 tsp]] salt and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and [[8 cups]] water, bring to a boil, then simmer, covered, for 30 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Lift out the chicken and shred the meat, discarding the bones. Return the meat to the pot.
For the dumplings, mix the cornmeal, cheese, egg, butter and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, adding 2 to 4 tablespoons warm water until it forms a firm dough.
Roll the dough into small balls the size of a walnut.
Drop the dough balls one by one into the simmering soup and cook for 15 minutes until they float and are firm.
Taste, adjust the salt and serve hot.
Mix the cassava starch, grated cheese and salt in a bowl, rubbing with your fingers until crumbly.
Add the melted butter, egg and milk and mix until the dough feels like damp sand.
Rest the mixture for 5 minutes.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat until hot. No oil is needed.
Spread a thick, even layer of the mixture, about 1/2 inch thick, over the pan without packing it down too much.
Cook 4 minutes until the underside is set and golden, then flip with a plate or large spatula.
Cook another 3 minutes until golden and the cheese is melted. Serve warm.
Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the beef in batches for 8 minutes. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot cook the onion, bell pepper and garlic for 5 minutes, then add the tomato and oregano.
Return the beef, add [[8 cups]] water and [[1.5 tsp]] salt, and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes until the beef is tender. Add the carrots for the last 20 minutes.
Mix the cornmeal, cheese, butter and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, adding warm water 1 tablespoon at a time to make a firm dough.
Roll the dough into small balls about 1 inch wide.
Drop the balls into the simmering broth and cook for 15 minutes until firm.
Season to taste and serve hot.
Cut the fish into 2-inch chunks and season with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, bell pepper and garlic for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they break down.
Pour in [[3 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt, bring to a simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the fish and cook gently for 8 minutes until it is opaque and flakes. Do not stir hard.
Pour in the milk and heat for 3 minutes without boiling.
Stir in the cheese, scatter parsley, and serve with rice or bread.
Rub the beef and pork with the coarse salt, garlic, pepper and oil. Let the meat sit at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C), or prepare a charcoal grill for low indirect heat.
Roast or grill the pork ribs for 1 hour 15 minutes, turning once, until tender and at least 145°F (63°C).
Add the beef short ribs after 30 minutes and cook 45 minutes more until browned and tender.
Meanwhile boil the cassava in salted water with [[8 cups]] water for 25 to 30 minutes until soft, then drain.
Grill or pan-fry the sausages for 15 minutes, turning, until the middle reaches 160°F (71°C).
Rest the meats for 10 minutes, cut into portions, and serve with the cassava and lemon wedges.

ing: beaten with 1 tbsp water, to brush
st: Mix the flour and [[1 tsp]] salt, then rub in the cold butter with your fingers until crumbly. Stir in the egg and warm water, knead briefly, wrap, and rest 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the beef and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until fully cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Stir in the cumin, paprika and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cool the filling for 15 minutes, then stir in the hard-boiled eggs and olives.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Roll the dough thin and cut 5-inch circles.
Place about [[2 tbsp]] filling on each circle, fold over, and crimp the edges with a fork.
Brush with the beaten egg yolk and bake on a lined sheet for 22 to 25 minutes until golden.
Cool slightly and serve warm. For fried empanadas, fry in 350°F (175°C) oil for 3 minutes per side.
Fill a large cup or guampa about two thirds full with the yerba mate.
Cover the top with your hand, tip the cup upside down, and shake gently so fine dust moves to the top.
Tip the cup back to a slant so the leaves bank against one side, leaving an open space.
Add the mint leaves and lemon slices next to the yerba, and some ice cubes.
Pour a little cold water in the empty space first to wet the leaves for 1 minute.
Place a metal straw with a filter into the damp side, and pour cold water slowly onto the leaves.
Sip until the water is gone, refilling with cold water and ice. Share the cup with friends.
